name: diff.zoo
title: Lags and Differences of zoo Objects

origin.usage: diff.zoo(x, lag = 1, differences = 1, arithmetic = TRUE, na.pad = FALSE, log = FALSE, ...)

arguments.name: lag
arguments.text: How many observations to look back. A negative lag looks forward.

arguments.name: differences
arguments.text: How many times to repeat the difference. Must be at least 1.

arguments.name: arithmetic
arguments.text: TRUE subtracts. FALSE uses a ratio, through logs when every value is positive.

arguments.name: na.pad
arguments.text: When TRUE, the original index is restored and the new times are NA.

arguments.name: log
arguments.text: When TRUE with arithmetic differences, subtract the logs and do not exponentiate.

origin.details: Each step subtracts lag(x, k = -lag) on the indexes the two series share, which drops the observations the lag removed. A positive series with arithmetic = FALSE is exp(log(x) - log(lag(x))). A series that is not entirely positive is divided instead. na.pad = TRUE merges an empty series that carries the original index.
origin.example:
x <- zoo(c(10, 20, 30, 40), 1:4)
z <- diff(x)
show <- function(v) paste(vapply(as.numeric(v), function(a) if (is.na(a)) "NA" else sprintf("%.16g", a), ""), collapse = " ")
cat(show(coredata(z)), "\n", sep = "")
cat(show(index(z)), "\n", sep = "")

translation.usage: diff_zoo(x, lag=1, differences=1, arithmetic=True, na_pad=False, log=False)

arguments.name: lag
arguments.text: How many observations to look back. A negative lag looks forward.

arguments.name: differences
arguments.text: How many times to repeat the difference. Must be at least 1. A fractional value is truncated the way R's colon operator truncates.

arguments.name: arithmetic
arguments.text: True subtracts. False uses a ratio, through logs when every value is positive.

arguments.name: na_pad
arguments.text: When True, the original index is restored and the new times are NaN.

arguments.name: log
arguments.text: When True with arithmetic differences, subtract the logs and do not exponentiate.

translation.details: Each step subtracts lag_zoo(x, k=-lag) on the indexes the two series share. A positive series with arithmetic=False is exp(log(x) - log(lag(x))). A series that is not entirely positive is divided instead. A missing value with arithmetic=False raises, because R's if() sees NA. na_pad=True merges an empty series that carries the original index.
translation.example:
import math
import numpy as np
from zoo.series import Zoo
from zoo.window import diff_zoo

def show(values):
    array = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    flat = array.reshape(-1, order="F") if array.ndim == 2 else array.reshape(-1)
    parts = []
    for value in flat:
        value = float(value)
        parts.append("NA" if math.isnan(value) else format(value, ".16g"))
    return " ".join(parts)

x = Zoo([10.0, 20.0, 30.0, 40.0], [1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0])
z = diff_zoo(x)
print(show(z.data))
print(show(z.index))
